notes: Garnet Hill is primarily a women's/girls' clothing and bedding/bath catalog; its Home Decor department is tiny. ACCESS: plain direct fetch and a bare curl_cffi GET both hit Akamai's edgesuite 'Access Denied' block; curl_cffi impersonate=chrome131 (also chrome110/116/120/124, safari17_0/18_0/18_0_ios, firefox133/135 - all tested OK per the prior session's ok_*.html sweep) got 200 on every category page. PLATFORM: same IBM WebSphere Commerce 'PWA' + Unbxd search-grid platform as Ballard Designs/Frontgate/Grandin Road/Company Store (Cornerstone Brands family) - body class view-UnbxdBodyView, static assets under /wcsstore/CornerStoneBrands/. CATEGORY TREE: enumerated from SiteMap_CAT_001-004_v2.xml (listed in SiteMapIndex_v2.xml, unprotected, ~140 URLs total) - full bedding-home tree is bath/, bedding/, decor/ (furniture, lighting, pillow-covers, decorative-accessories, throws), rugs/, collections/, features/, all-home/; clothing/shoes/swimwear trees are irrelevant. COUNTS: each category page's inline PWA.data.templateInfo JSON gives its numeric categoryId; GET https://www.garnethill.com/UnbxdAPI?categoryId=<id>&returnRespAsJSON=true&isAPI=true&requesttype=ajax&rows=200&unbxdStart=0 with header CBI-AJAX:1 (same request pattern as the Ballard/Frontgate precedent files) returns raw JSON with numberOfProducts and a products array - this is the exact storefront grid request, not a guessed vendor total. VERIFIED for the one qualifying category (Lighting, categoryId 191595): numberOfProducts=21, products array returned exactly 21 entries with 21 unique uniqueId values (base productIds repeat across color variants, e.g. Stella Ceramic Table Lamp has 6 color tiles, each counted as its own grid tile - matching how the storefront itself renders separate tiles per color), and a boundary check returned exactly 1 tile at unbxdStart=20 and 0 tiles at unbxdStart=21. All 21 titles read (table lamps, a lamp base, and a pair of wall sconces) - genuine lighting fixtures, no bulbs/fans. EXCLUDED after checking: Furniture (categoryId 191591, numberOfProducts=35, verified via same UnbxdAPI call) - all beds/nightstands/dressers/side tables/poufs/chairs, no mirrors or lighting mixed in, dropped as furniture. Decorative Accessories (categoryId 191598, numberOfProducts=7, verified) - read all 7 titles: Felted Doorstop, Bedding Storage Bag, Hand-Embroidered Pumpkins (holiday), Fall Wreath and Sunflower Wreath (faux/artificial wreaths, explicitly excluded), Wool Pouf (furniture/textile), and exactly one genuinely in-scope item, 'Scalloped-Edge Mirror Collection' (a mirror, in scope under Rule 0.3) - dropped as a mixed roll-up (6 of 7 out of scope) per the 'inspect actual titles, drop mixed roll-ups' rule; the single mirror SKU has no dedicated Mirrors category/URL anywhere on the site (confirmed no 'mirror' node exists in any of the 4 CAT sitemaps) so it cannot be extracted as its own row without inventing a URL - flagged here as a MANUAL REVIEW note only, not a row (same precedent as Frontgate's buried LED vanity mirrors). Also excluded: Pillow Covers and Throws (textiles), Bath (bath-rugs-mats/shower-curtains/towels - textiles/bath fixtures), Bedding (comforters/sheets/duvet-covers/quilts/shams/blankets-throws/bedding-basics - textiles), Rugs (area-rugs/doormats - textiles), All Home Decor (bedding-home/decor/ itself is the parent nav landing page, not a leaf listing), All Bedding & Home (bedding-home/all-home/, a 'shop everything' rollup - never-extract per Shop All rule), Collections and Features (marketing/curated pages), 50th Anniversary and New Arrivals and Sale/Clearance (marketing/re-cut pages). No clock, glassware, or tableware categories exist anywhere on this site. RULE 0: checked specifically for a Lighting-by-Room tree, bathroom/vanity/outdoor lighting nodes, and any mirror node under any room name - none exist; the single 'Lighting' category is undifferentiated by room, and Rule 0 room-based nodes simply are not part of this site's taxonomy, so Rule 0 did not add any rows here beyond confirming nothing was wrongly dropped for a room-word reason.
